Due to the short [half-life](/wiki/Half-life "Half-life") of all its isotopes, its natural occurrence is limited to tiny traces of the fleeting [polonium-210](/wiki/Polonium-210 "Polonium-210") (with a half-life of 138 days) in [uranium](/wiki/Uranium "Uranium") [ores](/wiki/Ore "Ore"), as it is the [penultimate daughter](/wiki/Decay_chain "Decay chain") of natural [uranium-238](/wiki/Uranium-238#Radium_series_(or_uranium_series) "Uranium-238"). Though two longer-lived isotopes exist (polonium-209 with a half-life of 124 years and polonium-208 with a half-life of 2.898 years), they are much more difficult to produce. Some crocus species, known as "autumn crocus", flower in late summer and autumn, during (autumnal) rains, after summer's heat and drought. The name **autumn crocus** is also often used as a common name for *[Colchicum](/wiki/Colchicum "Colchicum")*,[[68]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWyman1986-70) which is not a true crocus but in its own family ([Colchicaceae](/wiki/Colchicaceae "Colchicaceae")) in the lily order [Liliales](/wiki/Liliales "Liliales"). The plants are toxic, but have medicinal uses. *Colchicum* are also known as **meadow saffron**, though true [saffron](/wiki/Saffron "Saffron") is not toxic.[[69]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGBIF2022-71) *Crocus* species have three stamens while *Colchicum* species have six;[[70]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmitage2008278-72) crocus have one style, while *Colchicum* have three.[[71]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBowles1985154-73)[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMabberley1997-10)

Some [Pulsatilla](/wiki/Pulsatilla "Pulsatilla") species are also called "prairie crocus" (previously *[Anemone patens](/wiki/Pulsatilla_patens "Pulsatilla patens"))* or "wild crocus", but they belong to the buttercup family ([Ranunculaceae](/wiki/Ranunculaceae "Ranunculaceae")).[[72]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERunkelRoosa20097-74)[[73]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESkelly1994-75) Pulsatilla species, which are commonly called pasqueflowers, unlike crocuses have [rhizomes](/wiki/Rhizome "Rhizome"), the foliage is covered with long soft hairs, and the flowers are produced on above-ground stems.[[74]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWencaiBartholomew2004-76)[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmitage2008843-77)
